text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code to a shared repository, and automated builds start immediately. This means the system compiles the code and runs tests without any manual work. By running tests automatically, teams can catch issues early, before they become serious problems. This saves time and reduces stress. CI pipelines often include several stages, such as building, testing, and checking code quality. When something fails, the team gets quick feedback and can fix it fast. As a result, software stays more reliable and releases become smoother and more predictable.
